The agency recognizes that there is some merit to each of these positions on the relationship between the AFES program and the measures to improve average fuel economy that will be taken up to MY 1979. The correct viewpoint is probably at some indeterminate point between these extremes.
Fuel economy test procedures for MY 1979 are different from those in effect for MY 1976. A vehicle tested to both procedures would likely show a lower reported fuel economy for the MY 1979 test procedures. Fuel savings described in this EIS were determined based on a comparison of fuel economies for the MY 1976 procedures. If the MY 1979 procedures produce results closer to real-world experience and result in lower reported fuel economy, all other things being equal, the actual savings would be more than described in the EIS. For example, if the fuel economy penalty for the MY 1979 test procedures is 10 percent, the MY 1976 production weighted fuel economy would be 14.5 mpg based on MY 1979 procedures rather than the 16.1 mpg used in this EIS.
